title: Residency handoff & rollback checklist
summary: Practical operator-focused checklist and decision criteria for handing off region-pinning changes to oncall and for rolling back failed pin/migration operations. Emphasizes telemetry signals, customer comms, and edge-cache considerations.
content:
Context:
This doc is meant to live alongside the residency enforcement playbooks. It is intentionally terse and operator-centric: concise checklists, clear rollback gates, and exact telemetry to inspect. Use when handing over a region-pin change to oncall or when executing a rollback after an incident during a pin rollout or migration.

High-level objective:
- Minimize customer impact during pin changes and migrations
- Provide deterministic rollback/runforward gates with measurable signals
- Reduce ambiguity for oncall and SRE executing the handoff or rollback

When to use this doc:
- Customer region pin scheduled change (maintenance window)
- Automated migration push with new routing policy
- Emergency rollback after increased error rate or residency violations

Pre-handoff checklist (to run before the change leaves engineering working hours):
- Confirm change owner and primary oncall contact (name + pager).
- Attach the change to ticket (JIRA-4567) and link the canary run artifacts.
- List impacted tenants (tenant IDs + account owner emails).
- Verify rollback bundle prepared: rollback config file, previous policy hash, SQL/DB revert script if any.
- Confirm telemetry dashboards pre-populated and shared: per-tenant latency, error rate, residency-evidence metric, KV-cache-hit, streaming-fallbacks.
- Prepare customer comm templates (pre/post windows and incident templates).
- Ensure runbook commands present and validated in staging (exact kubectl/ops CLI).

Operator handoff script (handover checklist to oncall):
1) Quick summary: which tenants are pinned, target region(s), reason for pin, expected impact.
2) Location of change artifacts: PR, config, rollback file.
3) Canary plan: percentage of traffic, duration, criteria to escalate.
4) Intuition-level risk score (low/medium/high) and worst-case rollback time estimate.
5) Slack channel and escalation contacts (Dev lead, SRE, Legal if cross-border).

Canary & monitoring gates (must be green to proceed):
- Latency P95 within +20% of baseline for 15m window.
- Token-level error rate (5xx) < 0.25% sustained in 15m.
- Residency-evidence pass rate (per-tenant) >= 99.9% for the canary slice.
- Edge cache consistency: key TTLs behaving (KV cache hit ratio >= expected).
- No increases in fallback-to-hosted traffic beyond threshold.
- No customer support tickets opened for affected tenants during canary window.

Rollback gates (criteria to roll back immediately):
- Any single tenant shows residency-evidence failures > 0.1% of requests in a 5m window.
- Latency P99 > 2x baseline or sustained P95 > allocation for 10m.
- Error rate spike resulting in degraded SLAs for customers.
- Unexpected cross-border routing detected by evidence logs.
- Operator cannot achieve consistent KV/cache sync between edge and origin within 30 minutes.

Rollback steps (ordered):
1) Trigger pre-baked rollback config (ops apply rollback-config --id <change-id>).
2) Reduce canary to zero traffic and re-route to previous policy.
3) Invalidate edge-level caches if consistency issues suspected (edge-cache invalidate --pattern tenant-<id>).
4) Run residency-evidence sweep for affected tenants and capture logs for audit.
5) Open incident in PagerDuty and assign to oncall lead with collected artifacts.
6) Notify customer-success and affected customers using incident template.
7) After stabilization, begin postmortem note collection and link to JIRA-4567.

Edge cache & TTL specific notes:
- For pinned tenants, we operate with shorter TTLs during migration windows (default 60s -> 10s) to reduce stale region evidence.
- Make TTL changes in two steps: step1 (canary group) then step2 (full rollout).
- If inconsistent edge eviction patterns observed, do targeted invalidation rather than global flush.

Telemetry & evidence collection (exact signals to attach to incident):
- residency_evidence.{tenant_id}.{request_id} (raw logs) — sample 1/100 requests for forensic analysis.
- routing_decision.log (contains input fingerprint and policy chosen).
- kv_cache.hit_ratio.{node_id} and kv_cache.eviction_rate.{node_id}.
- routing_fallbacks.count and fallback_reason tags.
- per-tenant latency histograms and error-trace IDs.

Customer comms (templates & timing):
- Pre-change: 48h notice for enterprise customers; SMS + email for pinned tenants.
- If rollback occurs: notify within 1 hour with short summary, impact window, and follow-up timeline.
- Postmortem: high-level timeline + remediation plan within 72h for impacted enterprise tenants.

Run-forward considerations (when rollback is NOT chosen):
- If issue is transient and within acceptable SLO degradation, escalate to eng to patch live (hotfix).
- If only edge-cache inconsistency, attempt targeted invalidation and continue canary.
- Document reasoning and record threshold breaches that were tolerated.

Evidence packaging for audits/legal: 
- For any action affecting residency, preserve evidence bundle: routing_decision.log snippet, residency_evidence sampling, config diffs, and ticket timeline.
- Use the standard packaging script: tools/package_residency_evidence.sh --change <id> --time-range <t0,t1>.

Troubleshooting quick commands (ops CLI snippets):
- Show current pin policy: ops routing show --tenant <tenant-id> --verbose
- Switch to previous policy: ops routing apply --file rollback-<change-id>.json
- Invalidate edge key: edgectl invalidate --pattern tenant-<tenant-id> --region eu-west-1
- Collect evidence sample: tools/evidence_sample.sh --tenant <id> --limit 1000 > /tmp/evidence.json

Post-incident followup checklist:
- Confirm rollback success and stable metrics for 24h.
- Create postmortem with RCA and corrective actions.
- If root cause is config drift or infra bug, schedule a fix and link PR.
- Adjust runbook thresholds if they were too sensitive/lenient.

Known open questions / TODOs:
- Determine acceptable default TTL during rolling pins (proposed: 15s) - @Priya to validate with infra.
- Automate evidence packaging on rollback (currently manual).
- Add a per-tenant grace window config for transient routing failures.

Appendix: example incident timeline (template)
- T0: change applied to canary (10% traffic).
- T0+10m: slight latency increase observed (P95 +12%).
- T0+18m: tenant-345 residency_evidence failures 0.2% -> trigger rollback.
- T0+22m: ops apply rollback-config -> canary reduced to zero.
- T0+30m: edge invalidation for tenant-345.
- T0+40m: metrics stabilize, incident declared resolved; customers notified.

Notes to self / operator tips:
- If you see cross-border evidence, collect both source and target routing_decision logs immediately; those are high fidelity.
- Prefer targeted invalidation over global cache flush during business hours.
- Keep a short list of enterprise contacts for rapid approvals.

If anything in this checklist is unclear during handoff, call the change owner directly rather than assuming defaults. This doc is intentionally prescriptive to reduce cognitive load during high-pressure rollbacks.

-- End of doc --
